key_insight: The paper reframes image editing as a geometry problem by using 3D boxes to explicitly define what changes should happen, rather than relying on vague text prompts or weak 2D controls. By specifying both the input and output boxes, users can guide large object motions and camera changes much more precisely.
problem_solved: It addresses the ambiguity of existing image-editing interfaces, which often struggle to control spatial transformations in real images—especially when objects move far or the viewpoint changes significantly.
method: Represent edits with 3D boxes as structured specifications instead of loose conditioning signals.
Provide the input box and desired output box to define the transformation directly.
Cast the editing task as a well-posed geometry problem for more reliable spatial control.
impact: This makes complex real-image edits more controllable and intuitive for practitioners working on generative editing, scene manipulation, and human-in-the-loop image editing. It can improve precision in applications where accurate object relocation and viewpoint changes matter.

paper_title: Thinking in Boxes: 3D Editing in Real Images Made Easy
paper_authors: Pradhaan S Bhat, Naveen Chandra R, Rishubh Parihar, Vaibhav Vavilala, R. Venkatesh Babu
